standard.title: Values, beliefs and identities
standard.description: analyse and reflect on the influence of values and beliefs on the development of identities
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explained how identities can be influenced by people and places, and how positive self-identities can be created (Y5-6). They can identify external influences on identity but have not yet been expected to analyse how values and beliefs specifically operate as mechanisms of influence.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and reflect on the influence of values and beliefs on the development of identities.

nodes.label: Understanding values and beliefs as identity influences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what values and beliefs are and describe how they can shape how a person sees themselves.
nodes.minimum_width: Define values and beliefs and give at least one example of how a personal or family value influences how a person sees themselves.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how values and beliefs from different sources (personal, family, peer, cultural) operate as influences on identity; describe specific mechanisms by which values and beliefs shape self-perception.
wider: Examine how cultural values and beliefs from diverse communities in Australia — including young Australians of Asian heritage — influence self-perception and identity in distinctive ways
Explore how digital culture and social media create new sites where values and beliefs about identity are negotiated and contested for young people
nodes.hinge_reason: Analysis requires a conceptual framework for what values and beliefs are and how they function — students who cannot distinguish values and beliefs from other identity influences cannot meaningfully analyse their specific role. Reflection on personal identity is equally dependent on this foundation.

response_modes.reason: Distinguish between values (what one believes is important) and beliefs (what one holds to be true) and model how each type of influence operates through specific examples before students attempt their own analysis.

success_criteria: Explains what values and beliefs are
Gives at least one example of how a value or belief influences how a person sees themselves

nodes.label: Analysing influence on identity development
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how specific values and beliefs — from personal, family, peer or cultural sources — influence identity development, identifying the mechanism of influence.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one source of values or beliefs (personal, family or cultural) and analyse how it influences identity development in at least one specific way.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how values and beliefs from multiple sources influence identity development across a range of contexts; examine how cultural beliefs about puberty, gender, and physical change specifically affect the development of gender, cultural and sexual identities.
wider: Analyse how naming of deceased protocols (such as kumanjayi) in First Nations Australian communities reflect community values and impact the identities of community members
Examine how cultural beliefs about puberty and physical change create different pathways to gender, cultural and sexual identity across different cultural communities

response_modes.reason: Analysis of identity influence deepens when students encounter culturally diverse examples — encountering how the same mechanism (values → identity) operates differently across cultural contexts builds genuine analytical capacity rather than culturally narrow conclusions.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cultural diversity in identity analysis examples develops cross-cultural empathy and analytical breadth — students who engage with First Nations and Asian Australian perspectives on identity develop a significantly richer analytical framework than those who only examine their own cultural context.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one source of values or beliefs and names the source (personal, family, peer or cultural)
Analyses at least one specific way that source influences identity development

nodes.label: Reflecting on personal identity development
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on how their own values and beliefs — and those of the people and communities around them — have contributed to their developing sense of identity.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one personal or family value or belief and reflect on one way it has shaped their own sense of identity.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on how values and beliefs from multiple sources (personal, family, friends, cultural community) have influenced their own identity development; connect this reflection to the broader analysis completed in prior nodes.
wider: Reflect on how navigating between different cultural value systems (e.g. for students with bicultural or multicultural backgrounds) has shaped their developing identity in distinctive ways
Investigate how their own values about identity compare to and differ from those of their family, peer group and cultural community, reflecting on what this reveals about identity negotiation

response_modes.reason: Reflection integrates the conceptual analysis of values/beliefs/identity with personal experience — instruction should position reflection as an application of the analytical framework, not as separate personal disclosure.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one personal, family or cultural value or belief that has influenced their own identity
Reflects on at least one specific way that value or belief has shaped their sense of self
